answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, externally acquired resource—such as a deposit or proof-of-work-backed credit—before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. The ledger binds that stake to one identity and slashes it when independently verified fraud is proven, so creating a thousand orchard, summit, or signal accounts does not create free influence: each must fund its own stake, and attackers risk losing it. The defense raises the cost of identities; it does not make Sybils impossible.
